title: Action Spectrum for Melatonin Regulation in Humans: Evidence for a Novel Circadian Photoreceptor
research_question: To establish an action spectrum for light-induced melatonin suppression in humans to elucidate the ocular photoreceptor system for regulating the human pineal gland.

participants.description: 37 females, 35 males, mean age 24.5 ± 0.3 years, healthy, normal color vision (Ishihara and Farnsworth Munsell D-100 tests), stable daily sleeping pattern, 18-30 years old. Ethnic distribution: 55 Caucasians, 9 Asians, 4 African Americans, 3 Hispanics, 1 unknown.
participants.recruitment: Volunteers who were involved in shift work, planned long-distance jet travel before or during the study period, or had irregular sleeping schedules were excluded from this study.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Full-field, monochromatic light exposures (420, 440, 460, 480, 505, 530, 555, 575, 600 nm) delivered via a ganzfeld apparatus. Light irradiances ranged from 10^10 to 10^14 photons/cm² (4 log unit photon density range). Pupils were dilated (0.5% cyclopentolate HCl). Exposure duration was 90 minutes (2:00-3:30 A.M.).

measures.instrument: Miniature video camera inside ganzfeld dome
Tektronix J16 Radiometer/Photometer with J6512 irradiance probe, ft-1° meter (Minolta), portable spectroradiometer (Ocean Optics S2000)

findings.antecedent: Monochromatic light exposure at 460 nm (irradiances at 2.3 μW/cm² and lower)
findings.quote: At 460 nm, exposure to irradiances of 2.3 μW/cm² and lower did not significantly suppress plasma melatonin.

findings.antecedent: Monochromatic light exposure at 460 nm (irradiances at 3.1 μW/cm² and higher)
findings.quote: In contrast, exposures of 3.1 μW/cm² and higher elicited significant melatonin suppressions (p < 0.03 or less).

findings.consequent: Plasma melatonin percent control-adjusted change scores
findings.quote: one-way, repeated-measures ANOVA showed a significant effect of light intensity on plasma melatonin percent control-adjusted change scores (F = 14.92; p < 0.0001).

findings.antecedent: Monochromatic light exposure at 460 nm (irradiances at or above 3.1 μW/cm²)
findings.quote: Post hoc tests on plasma melatonin percent control-adjusted scores demonstrated that all intensities at or above 3.1 μW/cm² significantly suppressed melatonin more than the 0.012 μW/cm² stimulus (p < 0.05 or less).

findings.antecedent: Monochromatic light exposure at 460 nm (irradiances at or above 12.1 μW/cm²)
findings.quote: Similarly, all irradiances at or above 12.1 μW/cm² significantly suppressed melatonin more than the 1.5 μW/cm² stimulus.

findings.antecedent: Monochromatic light exposure at 460 nm (24.2 and 42.2 μW/cm²)
findings.consequent: Plasma melatonin percentage of control-adjusted change scores
findings.quote: Finally, both 24.2 and 42.2 μW/cm² exposures elicited significantly higher plasma melatonin percentage of control-adjusted change scores compared with 2.3 μW/cm².

findings.antecedent: Monochromatic light exposure at 420 nm (31.8 μW/cm²)
findings.quote: That decrease in melatonin was statistically significant (t = 4.67; p < 0.003).

findings.consequent: Potency for circadian input for melatonin regulation
findings.mechanism: This wavelength region corresponds to the peak spectral sensitivity (λmax = 464 nm) of a novel opsin photopigment.
findings.quote: identifies 446-477 nm as the most potent wavelength region providing circadian input for regulating melatonin secretion.

findings.antecedent: Action spectrum for light-induced melatonin suppression
findings.mechanism: The action spectrum fits a retinaldehyde opsin template, suggesting a retinaldehyde-based photopigment.
findings.quote: The action spectrum constructed from these data fit an opsin template (R2 = 0.91)

findings.antecedent: Action spectrum for light-induced melatonin suppression
findings.mechanism: The action spectrum predicted a peak spectral sensitivity (λmax) of 464 nm.
findings.quote: this action spectrum predicted a peak spectral sensitivity (λmax) of 464 nm.

findings.antecedent: Monochromatic light at 555 nm (equal photon density as 460 nm)
findings.mechanism: The photopic visual system (peak sensitivity ~555 nm) is not likely to be the primary input for circadian regulation, as 555 nm light is significantly weaker than 460 nm light in suppressing melatonin.
findings.quote: The results clearly demonstrate that 555 nm is significantly weaker in suppressing melatonin compared with an equal photon density of 460 nm.

findings.consequent: Match with action spectra for individual visual photoreceptor systems (rods and cones)
findings.mechanism: The photoreceptors mediating melatonin regulation are distinct from the known photoreceptors for vision.
findings.quote: Figure 6 shows that none of the action spectra for individual visual photoreceptor systems match the action spectrum for melatonin suppression.

findings.mechanism: High coefficients of correlation (0.99, 0.97, 0.95, 0.97, 0.98, 0.92, 0.96, and 0.97 respectively) indicate good fit.
findings.quote: wavelengths at 440, 460, 480, 505, 530, 555, 575, and 600 nm had respective coefficients of correlation (R²): 0.99, 0.97, 0.95, 0.97, 0.98, 0.92, 0.96, and 0.97.

findings.mechanism: High coefficients of correlation (0.91, 0.95, 0.93, 0.94, 0.92, 0.90, 0.95, and 0.81 respectively) indicate good fit to a univariant model.
findings.quote: When fit to a univariant fluence-response curve with these factors, the data from exposures to 440, 460, 480, 505, 530, 555, 575, and 600 nm have high coefficients of correlation of 0.91, 0.95, 0.93, 0.94, 0.92, 0.90, 0.95, and 0.81, respectively.

mechanisms: A novel opsin photopigment, distinct from rod and cone photoreceptors, mediates circadian photoreception in humans. This photopigment is retinaldehyde-based and has a peak spectral sensitivity between 446-477 nm (specifically 464 nm).
The univariance of the fluence-response curves suggests that a single photoreceptor type is primarily responsible for melatonin suppression.
moderators: Age (controlled by restricting participants to 18-30 years old to minimize lens pigmentation effects)
implementation_implications: Optimizing light therapy: Total illuminances for treating disorders can be reduced by optimizing the wavelength emissions of therapeutic equipment.
Architectural lighting: New approaches may be needed to optimally stimulate both visual and circadian systems, as the photoreceptors for these functions appear to be distinct.
limitations: The univariance of the fluence-response function at 420 nm is not certain because only one intensity was tested. A full fluence-response curve at 420 nm is needed to clarify precise sensitivity and confirm univariance.
Caution should be exercised in generalizing results from plants, insects, fish, amphibians, and rodents to humans.
It is not certain that there is a univariant fluence-response function at 420 nm because only one intensity has been tested.
